diagram_math_checks.objects_and_maps: The square has P at upper left, C at upper right, B at lower left, A at lower right. Its arrows are q:P→C, p:P→B, c:C→A and b:B→A, exactly the representatives/projections of step 1.1.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The Statement supplies monomorphisms b:B→A and c:C→A. def-pullbacks-and-pushouts defines a pullback for that cospan with projections to B and C.

diagram_math_checks.relation: Both paths P→A are typed; bp and cq have equal domain P and codomain A, and bp=cq.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The pullback defining equation in def-pullbacks-and-pushouts and revised step 1.1 explicitly assert this commutativity. The figure asserts no additional relations or maps.

diagram_math_checks.monomorphism_and_meet: p is the pullback of the monomorphism c along b, hence monic by [L2]; b is monic, so m=bp=cq:P→A is monic and factors through both subobject representatives.
diagram_math_checks.justification: The exact orientation matches the displayed square of lem-pullbacks-of-monomorphisms-are-monomorphisms-and-pushouts-of-epimorphisms-are-epimorphisms. Step 1.1 and [L3] give the lower-bound relation.

diagram_math_checks.universal_property: For any lower bound n:N→A, the factor maps u:N→B and v:N→C obey bu=cv=n. The universal property gives w:N→P with pw=u and qw=v, so mw=bu=n. Thus [n]≤[m], with the same factorisation order as the local [L3] supplier.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Step 1.2 proves this in full prose; step 2.1 concludes that m represents the meet. No inference requires interpreting the picture.
